analysis.title: GS Oil - Crude Vol Summary
key_insights: Crude implied vols and call skew have repriced after weeks of lagging the flat-price risk premium. 3m ATM vol is up 11.5 vols w/w.
Backend vols (H27-Z27) led the move. 1y ATM vol is at 3 year highs while the front remains well off the escalation highs.
The backend move came from producer hedging in the backend and spec downside put demand moving further out the curve.
Prompt put skew underperformed and calls rallied. Risk reversals remain subdued vs the 2026 lookback.
Positive spot-vol correlation has returned. Spec and macro accounts that had been largely absent are buying calls in size.
GS expects the call buying to have further room to run as the market prices post-midterm escalation risk over the coming weeks.

Dec implied daily breakevens finished around $3.5/bbl vs 20-day realised closer to $2/bbl, which looks expensive close-to-close. The average daily high-low range over the past 20 days is close to $4/bbl, so implied breakevens are less rich on that measure.
With Jan rolling into the prompt, $4/bbl Jan breakevens may be difficult to sustain. Front-month vol has been expiring in deep contango recently.
GS prefers holding vol length in the deferred against a small short in front-month vol.
1m Brent expires on 27 Oct. Marks are as of COB 26 Oct.

trade_ideas.description: Long deferred crude vol against a small short in front-month vol
